summary: Over 14 days with good CGM coverage, mean glucose was 121.6 mg/dL with 86.0% time in range, 8.9% above range, and 5.1% below range. Afternoon local-time highs were followed by evening and overnight lows. No carbohydrates were logged, so meals were handled by always-on SMB and UAM with Dynamic ISF, not by carb ratios. Competing explanations are not separated, so the profile and AAPS groups are kept and the next step is observation rather than a value change.

analysis_steps.findings: The 14-day Nightscout set is usable for glucose-pattern review. Coverage is 98.7% with a 5-minute cadence, 3995 valid entries, 10 gaps, and a largest gap of 65 minutes. The selected AAPS profile is complete and declared historically applicable. Insulin and loop samples are present, but meal composition cannot be reconstructed.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3995 valid CGM entries, coverage_percent 98.7, data_quality status good, 655 insulin entries totaling 275.95 U, full aaps_profile basal CR ISF target DIA and SMB blocks, profile_context historical_applicability yes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero carb entries and zero grams; empty carb_treatment_entries; meal_strategies empty; only representative treatments and 24 of 6214 device statuses.

analysis_steps.findings: Hypoglycemia is the binding constraint. Time below range is 5.1% with CV 32.6%. Local 01:00 time below range is 18.5% and local 19:00 is 15.3%, with extremes of 41 to 42 mg/dL. Highs cluster from late morning through late afternoon. Correction windows include both large drops after modest insulin and rises that look meal-confounded. Sampled IOB reached about 4.7 to 5.9 U.
analysis_steps.evidence: glucose_summary TBR 5.1% TAR 8.9% TIR 86.0% CV 32.6%; hourly_glucose_local hour 1 and hour 19; glucose_extremes 41 to 293 mg/dL; therapy_response_windows with 234 to 56 mg/dL and 264 to 96 mg/dL; loop IOB and variable_sens; GLP-1 notes; occlusion and pump error on 2026-08-19.
analysis_steps.dependencies: data_quality supports hourly glucose conclusions but not activity or hypo-treatment attribution.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No activity, exercise, or hypo-treatment flags; incomplete bolus-level timeline.

analysis_steps.findings: Scheduled basal is about 16.2 U/day versus about 19.7 U/day total insulin. Overnight glucose drifts from a local 23:00 average of 105.7 mg/dL to 90.6 mg/dL at 01:00 with high time below range, then stabilizes from 04:00 to 07:00. The 08:00 to 10:00 and 12:00 to 17:00 rises are not clean fasting basal defects. The 16:00 basal of 0.5 U/h is already the lowest segment under the afternoon highs, and the 18:00 to 19:00 crash occurs as basal steps back up, so a basal increase is not isolated as the cause.
analysis_steps.evidence: basal_segments 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.7, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7 U/h; targets 90 mg/dL overnight and 100 mg/dL from 08:00; hourly_glucose_local; cob 0 in sampled loop rows.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview forbids adding overnight insulin until evening IOB and target 90 are separated.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No fasting basal-test nights; no carb or activity logs; mid-period profile-switch notes.

analysis_steps.findings: CR is time-segmented but unused in sampled loop rows because no carbs were entered. Flat ISF 56 mg/dL/U with Dynamic ISF on produced much stronger effective sensitivity when high. DIA 10 h can carry afternoon and evening insulin into the overnight low window. Correction responses are inconsistent and often meal-confounded, so CR, ISF, and DIA cannot be isolated as single defects.
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_ratio_segments 13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5, 12.6 g/U; isf_segments 56 mg/dL/U; dia_hours 10; total_carbs_g 0; loop cob 0 and variable_sens about 28 to 124 mg/dL/U; therapy_response_windows.
analysis_steps.dependencies: basal_targets overnight lows may be IOB and DIA rather than CR; automation review is required before any ISF or DIA change.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal size, timing, or composition; insulin action curve not measured; u200 dilute and GLP-1 confound identifiability.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are on, with SMB always enabled, so the unused COB gates are idle rather than contradictory. Observed meal control is UAM-first. Configured SMB minutes of 15 and 20 are modest versus scheduled basal, but custom loop reasons show larger SMBs and UAM High Boost, so inventory minutes understate aggressiveness. High temporary targets of 135 mg/dL with high-temp SMB disabled may have held SMB during some rises. Further SMB strengthening is unsupported given evening and overnight lows.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled true, uam_enabled true, smb_always_enabled true, smb_with_cob_enabled false, smb_interval 3 min, max_smb_basal_minutes 15, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes 20; loop reasons with UAM, UAM High Boost, SMB equals 0.3 to 1.6; temporary targets 108 to 135 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview TBR constraint; profile ISF, DIA, and target 90 share the late-IOB pattern.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Custom boost logic is only visible in reason strings; temporary-target intent is not declared.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is off. Dynamic ISF is on at 70% and is the main automation amplifier, compressing effective ISF when glucose is high. Max basal 12 U/h and max IOB 25 U were not binding while sampled IOB was already 4.7 to 5.9 U. Carb-absorption settings were idle with zero COB. Automation is covering unlogged intake and can overshoot; it is not a clean case to raise basal or strengthen ISF.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled false; dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true; dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent 70%; variable_sens about 27.8 to 124; sensitivity_ratio often 1 and sometimes 0.79 to 0.94; max_basal 12 U/h; max_iob 25 U; min_5m_carbimpact 8; meal_max_absorption_hours 7.
analysis_steps.dependencies: ISF 56, DynISF 70%, SMB or UAM size, DIA 10 h, and overnight target 90 are one dependent cluster.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: DynISF versus static ISF cannot be separated from this package alone.

analysis_steps.findings: The user-declared meal strategy list is empty, so there is no declared prebolus time or immediate bolus percent. Observed execution matches that empty declaration: meals, if present, were unannounced and dosed by UAM, SMB, and small corrections. The recurring clock pattern is a late-morning rise, larger 12:00 to 17:00 highs, then 18:00 to 19:00 and overnight lows. Announcing carbs into the 16:00 CR of 10.5 g/U on top of current UAM and Dynamic ISF would stack insulin into the highest hypo-risk window.
analysis_steps.evidence: analysis_context meal_strategies empty and strategy_stable_for_period null; treatment_summary 0 g carbs; therapy_response_windows all Correction Bolus with is_extended_carbs false; hourly_glucose_local afternoon TAR then evening TBR.
analysis_steps.dependencies: CR unused; SMB and UAM plus DynISF and DIA 10 h explain both catch-up and late lows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No declared or logged carb amount, bite time, or bolus percent.

analysis_steps.findings: No e-carb amount, start offset, or duration is declared or logged. Extended carb entries are zero. Absorption settings were idle. E-carbs are not a pump extended bolus and were not used. Adding e-carbs on top of always-on UAM is not supported while evening and overnight time below range is elevated.
analysis_steps.evidence: extended_carb_entries 0; carb_treatment_entries empty; cob 0 in sampled loop rows; idle min_5m_carbimpact and meal_max_absorption_hours.
analysis_steps.dependencies: meal_bolus_strategy and automation_smb_uam; hypo risk after 18:00.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal-linked e-carb evidence and no meal composition.

analysis_steps.findings: The most coherent explanation is unannounced daytime intake handled late by UAM and Dynamic ISF, leaving residual IOB that lands on target 90 mg/dL overnight and also produces the 18:00 to 19:00 crash. Weaker competing explanations are slightly high overnight basal, weak afternoon basal, unused CR, and site or occlusion events. Because those causes are not separated, no profile or AAPS value change is supported in this cycle. Safe order is keep settings, collect carb timestamps, then consider only one later lever if low-IOB nights still show 01:00 lows.
analysis_steps.evidence: Combined hourly_glucose_local shape; zero carbs; DynISF-compressed variable_sens; IOB 4.7 to 5.9 U; TBR clusters; empty meal declaration; unresolved basal versus IOB versus target versus automation cluster.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Need timestamped carb entries and nights with documented low evening IOB to separate leftover meal insulin from overnight target or basal.

strengths: CGM coverage is good enough for hourly local-time pattern review.
Overall time in range is 86.0% with mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL.
Late-night to early-morning hours from about 04:00 to 08:00 local time are relatively stable with high time in range.
The selected profile is complete, and historical applicability is declared yes.
Autosens target shifting is off, so target changes are not being double-applied by Autosens.
High temporary-target SMB is disabled, which is a conservative brake during 135 mg/dL temporary targets.
issues: Time below range is 5.1%, with local 01:00 time below range 18.5% and local 19:00 time below range 15.3%, including glucose extremes of 41 to 42 mg/dL.
Afternoon local hours show repeated time above range, peaking near 16:00, then a crash into the evening low cluster.
No carbohydrates were logged, so carb ratios and absorption settings were idle and meals cannot be separated from UAM catch-up.
Profile ISF 56 mg/dL/U plus Dynamic ISF 70% produced much stronger effective sensitivity when high, and sampled IOB reached about 4.7 to 5.9 U while max IOB 25 U was not binding.
Custom loop UAM boosts mean configured SMB minutes understate observed aggressiveness.
A mid-period profile switch, u200 dilute notes, GLP-1 notes, and an occlusion with pump error add delivery and absorption noise.

recommendations.title: Keep the current profile and collect meal-timed observations first
recommendations.description: Afternoon highs and evening or overnight lows can be explained by unannounced intake, UAM catch-up, Dynamic ISF, DIA 10 h, and target 90 mg/dL. Those causes are not separated, so a profile value change is unsupported in this cycle.

suggested_change.next_observation: Log carbohydrate grams and time relative to first bite for several days, and review 01:00 glucose on nights with low evening IOB.
suggested_change.do_not_combine_with: No basal, ISF, DIA, target, SMB, or DynISF change in the same step.

recommendations.title: If low-IOB nights still show 01:00 lows, review overnight target before basal or SMB
recommendations.description: Raising overnight insulin or strengthening afternoon automation would fight the binding hypoglycemia pattern. If later nights with little evening IOB still sit below the 90 mg/dL target around 01:00, overnight target is the first conservative single lever to review, not a higher 16:00 basal and not more SMB.

suggested_change.later_review_direction: Consider a higher overnight target only after low-IOB nights are observed.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep the current profile, including overnight target 90 mg/dL and all basal, CR, ISF, and DIA values. The next action is observation, not a setting change.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Local 01:00 time below range is high near target 90 mg/dL, but leftover UAM and Dynamic ISF IOB, DIA 10 h, unlogged meals, and overnight basal are not separated. Changing target, basal, or ISF together would mix dependent effects. Safety data also argue against adding insulin to chase afternoon highs.
profile_recommendation.next_check: For several days, enter carbohydrate grams and clock time at first bite, then compare 00:00 to 03:00 glucose on nights when evening IOB is low versus nights after large afternoon UAM or correction IOB.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: local 00:00 to 01:00 averages fall toward 90.6 mg/dL with hour-1 time below range 18.5%, which can look like overnight insulin pressure. Uncertainty: the same window is the landing zone for evening UAM, corrections, and DIA 10 h. Dependencies: do not lower this basal in the same cycle as target, ISF, DynISF, or SMB changes; a fasting low-IOB night is required first.

Evidence: local 04:00 to 07:00 averages are about 99 to 106 mg/dL with high time in range and low time below range. Uncertainty: partial last and first days and site or sensor changes can still affect single mornings. Dependencies: this segment is not the 08:00 to 10:00 rise, which is more consistent with unannounced intake than a basal defect.

Evidence: local 06:00 to 08:00 stays near 99 to 110 mg/dL with very high time in range before the later morning rise. Uncertainty: no fasting basal test isolates this 0.8 U/h step from breakfast-timed intake. Dependencies: changing 06:00 basal would confound the 08:00 target step and morning UAM review.

Evidence: local 10:00 to 15:00 shows rising averages and more time above range while cob is 0 in sampled loop rows. Uncertainty: meals, temporary targets, and UAM lag remain plausible. Dependencies: this segment cannot be raised while the 18:00 to 19:00 low cluster is unexplained.

Evidence: this is already the lowest basal under the highest afternoon averages and 32.1% time above range at local 16:00. Uncertainty: unlogged intake and late UAM are equally able to create that rise. Dependencies: raising 16:00 basal would stack on DynISF-boosted SMBs and points at the 18:00 to 19:00 time-below-range cluster.

Evidence: local 18:00 average 124.2 mg/dL already includes 7.7% time below range as glucose is falling. Uncertainty: this looks more like arriving IOB than a unique basal step defect. Dependencies: linked to 16:00 UAM catch-up, DIA 10 h, and the following 19:00 basal step.

Evidence: local 19:00 has 15.3% time below range and extremes of 41 to 42 mg/dL, but basal is only stepping from 0.6 to 0.7 U/h. Uncertainty: residual afternoon insulin, unknown activity, and GLP-1 notes are competing causes. Dependencies: do not increase this segment while evening hypoglycemia is the binding safety issue.

Evidence: treatment_summary shows 0 g carbs and sampled loop rows show cob 0, so this CR was unused. Uncertainty: overnight lows cannot be attributed to CR. Dependencies: CR review requires timestamped carb entries and must not be combined with SMB or DynISF changes.

Evidence: no carb treatments exist in this window; early-morning glucose is relatively stable. Uncertainty: a stronger dawn CR cannot be validated without breakfast logs. Dependencies: unused CR plus UAM means any future announcement would stack on automation.

Evidence: the 08:00 to 10:00 rise occurs with cob 0, so this CR did not dose those events. Uncertainty: whether that rise is breakfast remains unproven. Dependencies: do not tighten CR to chase an unannounced pattern while evening hypoglycemia risk is high.

Evidence: this is the strongest CR, but it was idle; afternoon highs were followed by 18:00 to 19:00 lows after UAM and corrections. Uncertainty: if carbs were later entered here, 10.5 g/U plus DynISF and UAM could overfill IOB. Dependencies: meal announcement and this CR must not be introduced together with more SMB strength.

Evidence: evening time below range is already elevated and no evening carbs were logged. Uncertainty: leftover afternoon IOB versus any late snack cannot be split. Dependencies: overnight target 90 mg/dL and DIA 10 h make extra evening meal insulin a hypo risk.

Evidence: flat ISF 56 mg/dL/U with Dynamic ISF 70% produced variable_sens far from 56, and some corrections dropped 100 to 180 mg/dL. Uncertainty: afternoon highs still occur, so weakening or strengthening ISF both remain plausible until meals are logged. Dependencies: ISF, DynISF 70%, SMB size, and DIA are one cluster and must not change together.

Evidence: overnight target 90 mg/dL sits under the 01:00 low cluster. Uncertainty: leftover evening IOB may be the driver rather than the target number itself. Dependencies: this is the first later review lever only after low-IOB nights are observed; do not change it with basal or ISF in the same step.

Evidence: daytime target 100 mg/dL already sits above the overnight 90 mg/dL target while afternoon time above range continues. Uncertainty: some 135 mg/dL temporary targets may have held SMB. Dependencies: lowering this target would add insulin pressure against the evening low pattern.

Evidence: local 23:00 already has 10.1% time below range before the 01:00 trough. Uncertainty: this may reflect arriving IOB from the evening rather than the 23:00 target step alone. Dependencies: keep aligned with target 00:00; any later overnight target review should treat 23:00 and 00:00 as one night block.

Evidence: DIA 10 h can keep afternoon and evening insulin active into 00:00 to 03:00, matching the late low pattern. Uncertainty: insulin_type is free_peak_oref and a u200 dilute note exists, so true action duration is not measured. Dependencies: shortening DIA would change IOB accounting for SMB and corrections and must not be paired with ISF or DynISF edits.

Evidence: with 0 g carbs, SMB plus UAM was the meal engine and cob remained 0, so UAM was not double-counting COB. Uncertainty: the same pair also explains late IOB. Dependencies: disabling or strengthening this pair would confound CR, ISF, and target interpretation; no source component is null so verify is not used.

Evidence: always-on SMB makes COB gates idle, which matches zero carb entries; high-temp SMB off is consistent with 135 mg/dL temporary targets acting as a brake. Uncertainty: that brake may also contribute to some midday time above range. Dependencies: do not enable more SMB paths while time below range is 5.1%.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: configured 3, 15, and 20 minutes look modest versus 0.5 to 0.8 U/h basal, but reason strings show larger custom UAM boosts and SMBs. Uncertainty: changing inventory minutes may not change the custom boost path. Dependencies: SMB size, DynISF, and ISF must not be edited together.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: sampled IOB of about 4.7 to 5.9 U and requested rates around 3 to 4 U/h show these caps were not binding and did not create the lows. Uncertainty: they also did not prevent high IOB from custom boosts. Dependencies: tightening limits would be a later guardrail discussion, not a fix for unlogged meals or DynISF, and is not isolated enough to change now.

Evidence: Autosens is declared false; a sensitivity_ratio of 1 is a neutral current adjustment, not enabled Autosens. Dynamic ISF 70% compressed effective ISF when high and is a leading overshoot amplifier. Uncertainty: afternoon time above range still occurs, so more DynISF is unsupported and less DynISF is not isolated from unlogged meals. Dependencies: do not change DynISF in the same step as profile ISF, SMB minutes, or target.

Evidence: these settings were idle because no carbs and no e-carbs were entered. Uncertainty: they cannot be blamed for time above or below range. Dependencies: absorption model review only becomes relevant after carb entries exist; e-carbs are not an extended bolus and should not be added on top of full UAM now.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: There is no declared prebolus time and no declared immediate bolus percent. Keep meals unannounced or, if carbs are later entered, do not also rely on full UAM plus the 16:00 CR of 10.5 g/U. Keep current SMB and UAM as the observed meal engine only while watching evening IOB. Do not add e-carbs.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The user-declared meal_strategies list is empty, and telemetry shows 0 g carbs, no e-carbs, and cob 0. The recurring pattern is afternoon catch-up insulin then evening and overnight lows, so more immediate meal insulin is not isolated as helpful.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Enter carbohydrate grams and the clock time of first bite for several days, including whether a 135 mg/dL temporary target was intended as eating-soon.

exceptions.pattern: Local 12:00 to 17:00 rise then 18:00 to 19:00 crash
exceptions.suggestion: Do not add afternoon announcement, e-carbs, or stronger SMB to chase this rise until evening IOB is reviewed.
exceptions.rationale: This shape matches late UAM and Dynamic ISF IOB more than a validated CR or e-carb duration.

exceptions.suggestion: Treat as a smaller unannounced-meal proxy, not a separate prebolus or CR proof.
exceptions.rationale: The rise is less followed by immediate severe time below range than the afternoon pattern, and no breakfast carbs were logged.

implementation_steps: Review this as decision-support only. Independently verify every value against the pump and AAPS screens before touching settings.
Keep the current profile and the six AAPS groups unchanged for this cycle so dependent effects stay separable.
Start timestamped carbohydrate logging, including grams and time relative to first bite, and note why any temporary target was set.
Watch local 18:00 to 03:00 glucose together with evening IOB before considering any insulin-adding idea for afternoon highs.
If several nights with low evening IOB still show 01:00 lows near target 90 mg/dL, discuss overnight target as a single later review item, not a basal increase.
Only after that observation, consider whether profile ISF or Dynamic ISF 70% should be reviewed as one lever, never both at once and never with SMB minute changes.
Leave e-carbs and full CR announcement last. If carbs are entered, reduce reliance on UAM rather than stacking both.
education: UAM responds to an unexplained glucose rise and is not the same as entered carbs or a second COB pool.
A sensitivity_ratio of 1 is a neutral current adjustment. Autosens in this profile is off.
Dynamic ISF can make effective sensitivity much stronger than the profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U when glucose is high.
DIA 10 h means insulin from afternoon UAM or corrections can still be active overnight.
E-carbs are a carb-absorption signal for the algorithm, not a pump extended bolus.
Remaining time on a temporary basal or an SMB waiting message is not the configured 3-minute SMB interval.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. It is not medical advice and it does not change AAPS automatically.
Independently verify every proposed change, make at most one change at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
Time below range of 5.1% and extremes of 41 to 42 mg/dL limit any idea that adds overnight or evening insulin.
Sampled IOB reached about 4.7 to 5.9 U while max IOB 25 U was not protective.
An occlusion and pump error were logged on 2026-08-19; delivery failures can mimic profile or automation problems.
Discuss any setting review with the diabetes care team before changing insulin delivery.
